about: The three pairs of large salivary glands (parotid, submandibular, sublingual) with their ducts, the many minor glands of the mouth lining, the facial nerve plexus inside the parotid, the parasympathetic supply, and one magnified diagram of a salivary acinus with its duct system. Saliva volume is not simulated, so the only drives are the directions textbooks give: parasympathetic outflow raises secretion and sympathetic outflow raises it slightly, as a thick saliva. The weights are a display scale and the index is not a flow rate. Duct courses, lobule counts and the acinus are schematic; the acinus is magnified and placed in the middle of the organ, not at true size or position.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Parotid Glands
parts.summary: Largest pair, in front of and below each ear
parts.function: Each parotid lies against the cheek in front of the ear and drains by a duct that opens inside the cheek. Its saliva is thin and watery and rich in digestive enzyme. It brightens with parasympathetic outflow.

drives.note: Parasympathetic nerves stimulate the salivary glands to secrete.

parts.label: Superficial Part of the Parotid
parts.summary: The part lateral to the facial nerve plexus
parts.function: It forms most of the gland that can be felt in front of the ear.

parts.label: Deep Part of the Parotid
parts.summary: The part medial to the facial nerve plexus
parts.function: It lies deep to the nerve plexus, against the structures beside the throat.

parts.label: Parotid Duct (Stensen)
parts.summary: The duct that carries saliva from the parotid into the mouth
parts.function: It runs forward across the cheek and pierces the cheek muscle to open opposite the upper second molar.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation produces a copious watery saliva.

parts.label: Submandibular Glands
parts.summary: Pair under the body of the jaw
parts.function: Each gland lies beneath the jaw and drains by a duct that opens beside the tongue's frenulum. It makes a mixed watery and mucous saliva. It brightens with parasympathetic outflow.

drives.note: Parasympathetic nerves stimulate the salivary glands to secrete.

parts.label: Submandibular Duct (Wharton)
parts.summary: The duct that carries saliva from the submandibular gland to the floor of the mouth
parts.function: It runs forward above the mylohyoid and opens on the sublingual caruncle beside the frenulum.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation produces a copious watery saliva.

parts.label: Sublingual Glands
parts.summary: Smallest pair, in the floor of the mouth
parts.function: Each gland sits under the tongue and opens through many small ducts. Its saliva is mostly mucus, which lubricates the mouth. It brightens with parasympathetic outflow.

drives.note: Parasympathetic nerves stimulate the salivary glands to secrete.

parts.label: Sublingual Ducts
parts.summary: The many small ducts of the sublingual gland
parts.function: They open along the sublingual fold, and some join the submandibular duct.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation produces a copious watery saliva.

parts.label: Minor Salivary Glands
parts.summary: Hundreds of tiny glands in the lining of the mouth
parts.function: They lie in the lips, cheeks, palate and tongue and keep the mouth moist between meals. Their counts here are schematic.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation produces a copious watery saliva.

parts.label: Labial Glands
parts.summary: Small glands in the lips
parts.function: They open onto the inner surface of the lips.

parts.label: Buccal Glands
parts.summary: Small glands in the cheeks
parts.function: They open onto the inside of the cheek.

parts.label: Palatine Glands
parts.summary: Mucous glands in the palate
parts.function: They lie in the palate and make a mucous saliva.

parts.label: Lingual Glands
parts.summary: Glands in the tongue
parts.function: Some open into the trenches of the vallate papillae and wash the taste buds.

parts.label: Intraparotid Facial Plexus
parts.summary: The branches of the facial nerve inside the parotid gland
parts.function: The facial nerve passes through the gland and divides into branches that supply the muscles of facial expression. It does not supply the gland itself.

parts.label: Temporofacial Division
parts.summary: The upper division of the facial nerve
parts.function: It gives branches that run upward and forward over the face.

parts.label: Cervicofacial Division
parts.summary: The lower division of the facial nerve
parts.function: It gives branches that run forward and down over the face and neck.

parts.label: Parasympathetic Supply
parts.summary: The nerve pathways that drive secretion
parts.function: Fibres synapse in two ganglia: the otic ganglion for the parotid, and the submandibular ganglion for the submandibular and sublingual glands.

drives.note: These are the parasympathetic pathways that stimulate the glands.

parts.label: Otic Ganglion
parts.summary: The relay for the parotid gland
parts.function: Fibres from the glossopharyngeal nerve relay here and reach the parotid through a branch of the mandibular nerve.

parts.label: Submandibular Ganglion
parts.summary: The relay for the submandibular and sublingual glands
parts.function: It hangs from the lingual nerve and receives fibres that come from the facial nerve through the chorda tympani.

parts.label: Salivary Acinus (enlarged schematic)
parts.summary: A terminal secretory unit and its ducts, drawn magnified
parts.function: This is a microscopic structure drawn as a magnified diagram in the middle of the organ, not at true size or position. Saliva is made in the acini and modified as it passes along the ducts.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation produces a copious watery saliva.
Sympathetic stimulation produces only a small amount of thick saliva.

parts.label: Serous Acinar Cells
parts.summary: Cells that make a watery, enzyme-rich secretion
parts.function: They form round acini and are the main cell of the parotid.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation produces a copious watery saliva.

parts.label: Mucous Acinar Cells
parts.summary: Cells that make a thick, mucus-rich secretion
parts.function: They are common in the sublingual gland and lubricate the mouth.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation produces a copious watery saliva.

parts.label: Serous Demilunes
parts.summary: Crescents of serous cells capping a mucous acinus
parts.function: They add a watery secretion to a mucous acinus.

parts.label: Myoepithelial Cells
parts.summary: Contractile cells that embrace the acinus
parts.function: They squeeze the acinus and the duct to expel the saliva.

drives.note: Parasympathetic stimulation makes the gland secrete and the cells squeeze saliva out.

parts.label: Intercalated Duct
parts.summary: The first and narrowest duct from the acinus
parts.function: It carries the secretion from the acinus to the striated duct.

parts.label: Striated Duct
parts.summary: The duct whose cells alter the saliva
parts.function: Its cells adjust the salts in the saliva as it passes. Their folded bases give the striated look.

parts.label: Excretory Duct
parts.summary: The large duct that leaves the gland
parts.function: It joins others and carries the saliva to the mouth.
